vagueSymptom: After I recalculate this checkout, free shipping sometimes turns into a $19 charge even though the cart still says it qualifies.
plantedCondition: The runtime tax-calculation response adds a top-level shipping field with value 19.00; the public generic merge applies that later response after the valid zero-dollar shipping quote.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: The tax-calculation endpoint supplies the conflicting data.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: The shipping quote is independently valid and is not the source of the displayed charge.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: Its top-level shipping field has the value 19.00.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: The specific unexpected field and value identify the planted condition.

requiredDiagnosisFacts.fact: The generic merge overwrites the valid zero-dollar shipping quote with the tax response's shipping value.
requiredDiagnosisFacts.why: This explains why qualification remains visible while the combined summary charges for shipping.

requiredEvidence.evidence: Replacing only the tax response with the same payload minus shipping removes the charge on a repeated recalculation.
requiredEvidence.why: This response-mock counterfactual establishes the tax response as the cause.

requiredEvidence.evidence: Replacing the shipping response without changing the tax response does not remove the charge on a repeated recalculation.
requiredEvidence.why: This negative control rules out the plausible shipping-rule or shipping-quote explanation.

plausibleWrongAnswer: A shipping-threshold or postcode-eligibility rule rejects the cart.
